Introduction & Reproductive Health

Midwifery in nursing — midwifery, obstetrics, reproductive health and the role of the midwife.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define midwifery and obstetrics
  • Describe reproductive health concepts
  • Describe the legal basis of midwifery in India
  • List the roles of the midwife

In simple words

Midwifery is care of the woman during pregnancy, labour, birth, postnatal period and newborn. Obstetrics is the medical specialty for pregnancy and childbirth — midwifery is the nursing side of that care.

Reproductive health

Reproductive health means complete physical, mental and social wellbeing in all matters of the reproductive system — not absence of disease only.

  • Includes fertility, safe pregnancy and birth, contraception, prevention and treatment of infertility, and management of problems
  • Sexual and reproductive rights of women must be respected

Legal and policy basis in India

  • Indian Nursing Council Act, 1947 — midwifery education and registration
  • INC Curriculum — prescribes midwifery training and clinical practice
  • MTP Act — legal conditions of safe termination of pregnancy
  • PCPNDT Act — prevents sex determination
  • Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques protect women and prevent female foeticide
  • The Clinical Establishments Act ensures standards of care

Birth attendance: institutional vs home

Birth should be institutional. Institutions have equipment, skilled staff and referral. Home births need a trained attendant, referral plan, warm environment and infection prevention.

🔴 Skilled birth attendance saves lives

Most maternal deaths come from haemorrhage, sepsis, hypertensive disorders and obstructed labour. A trained midwife with a referral plan prevents deaths.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Midwifery is care before, during and after birth plus the newborn.
  2. Reproductive health is complete physical, mental and social wellbeing in reproduction.
  3. Institutional birth is promoted with referral for complications.
  4. Four major causes of maternal death: haemorrhage, sepsis, hypertension, obstructed labour.
  5. PCPNDT Act prevents sex determination.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. The midwife is an educator, advocate and care giver.
  2. Skilled birth attendance at every birth is the goal of SDG.
  3. Trained dais are supported and linked to health system.
  4. Birth planning includes transport and blood availability.
  5. Adolescent care tracks nutrition and legal consent.

📌 Memory trick

Maternal killers: H-S-H-O — Haemorrhage, Sepsis, Hypertensive disorders, Obstructed labour.

60-second revision

  • Midwifery: antenatal, intrapartum, postpartum and newborn care.
  • Obstetrics is the medical side; midwifery the nursing side.
  • Legal: INC Act 1947, MTP, PCPNDT, Clinical Establishments Act.
  • Aim: institutional birth with a trained midwife.
  • Major causes of maternal death: haemorrhage, sepsis, hypertension, obstructed labour.

Test yourself

The main sign of true labour is:

Answer: B. True labour shows progressive cervical effacement and dilatation with regular contractions.

Midwifery covers care during:

Answer: B. Midwifery covers antenatal, intrapartum, postpartum and newborn care.

The MTP Act deals with:

Answer: A. The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act defines the legal conditions for safe abortion.

The greatest single cause of maternal death worldwide is:

Answer: B. Postpartum haemorrhage is the leading direct cause of maternal death.

Birth is best attended:

Answer: B. Institutional birth with skilled attendance gives access to emergency obstetric care.
